correctness.rationale: Exact eigenvalue laws are probabilities, optimal symbol difference is their L1 distance. Laplace expansion at a strictly convex saddle yields L1 Gaussian convergence with controlled tails; center derivative du/dm=2s² and q=o(m) yields separation 2qs. Unit-normal L1 distance is 4Φ(qs)−2, with separated-window argument for infinity. Disjoint sparse logarithmic bumps with radius derivatives decaying establish one smooth sharp witness. Finite quadratures independently check constants but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The closest 2026 work exhibited metric failure for a single power-log exponent, but did not determine the universally sharp local index metric and Gaussian crossover or show the maximal defect persists for a globally smooth bounded symbol. The theorem gives an exact quantitative phase diagram: α<2 complete adjacent separation, α=2 fixed adjacent deficit, α>2 a nontrivial m^β smoothing threshold. This clarifies the metric structure relevant to radial Toeplitz eigenvalue algebras and is more than a routine parameter substitution.
